**MEMORANDUM**

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 10, 2026
**Re:** Zaseil Technical Fabrics, Inc. / Prodous Coating Services LLC: Review of contract package (MSA, SOW No. 1, Parent Guaranty, Order Form No. 3, Mutual NDA)
**Privileged & Confidential: Attorney Work Product**

---

## I. Executive Summary

I reviewed all five documents in the folder:

- the Master Services Agreement dated March 2, 2026 (Delaware law, §16.1) (**MSA**);
- Statement of Work No. 1 dated April 6, 2026 (**SOW No. 1**);
- the Parent Guaranty dated March 2, 2026 from **Prodous Industrial Holdings, Inc.**, as Guarantor (**Guaranty**);
- Order Form No. 3 dated October 20, 2026 (**OF3**); and
- the Mutual NDA dated January 12, 2026 (**NDA**).

I found four significant issues. Two need action within days.

| Rank | Issue | Location | Urgency | Whose agreement is needed to fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Third-party bodily injury and property damage indemnity is **capped** by SOW No. 1, and the SOW controls | SOW No. 1 §9.2 (read with MSA §§1.3, 11.2, 11.3(a)) | High. This is Zaseil's largest structural exposure | Prodous (amend SOW) |
| 2 | Guaranty 45-day Demand window for the Lot 2207 default **expired on September 17, 2026**, and no Demand has been made | Guaranty §4.1 (read with OF3 Special Terms ¶2) | Immediate | Guarantor (written waiver or acknowledgment) |
| 3 | Kestrel merger is a **Change of Control** that is deemed an assignment needing Prodous's prior written consent. No consent has been obtained | MSA §14.3 (read with §14.1, OF3 §2.5 and ¶1) | Immediate. Closing is expected December 1, 2026 | Prodous (written consent/waiver) |
| 4 | Prodous may **assign freely to anyone**, including a Zaseil competitor, and any permitted assignment **automatically terminates the Guaranty** | MSA §14.2; Guaranty §6.2 | High, but latent | Prodous (MSA) and Guarantor (Guaranty) |

**Ranking basis.** I ranked by the size of Zaseil's potential loss, with time-sensitivity as a tiebreaker.

- **Issue 1** is ranked first because an FR coating failure that leads to a fire injury is the catastrophic scenario for this relationship. SOW No. 1 currently caps Prodous's indemnity for that scenario at roughly one year of SOW fees.
- **Issues 2 and 3** are the most time-critical. They should be worked in parallel this week.

The NDA is not a source of any issue (see Part IV).

---

## II. Issues (Ranked)

### Issue 1: SOW No. 1 subjects Prodous's third-party injury and property damage indemnity to the Liability Cap

**Where:**
- SOW No. 1 §9.2, with §9.1;
- MSA §10.1(a), §11.2, §11.3(a) and §1.3.

**What the documents say.**

- **MSA §10.1(a).** Prodous must defend and indemnify Zaseil, its Affiliates and its *customers* against third-party Claims for bodily injury (including death) and property damage caused by the Services, the Finished Goods as processed, or "any failure of the FR coatings applied by Provider to meet the Specifications."
- **MSA §11.3(a).** This indemnity is carved out of both the Liability Cap (§11.2) and the consequential damages exclusion (§11.1).
- **SOW No. 1 §9.2.** It reverses that carve-out. "With respect to Section 11.3(a) of the MSA, for Claims arising from Coating Services performed under this SOW, Provider's indemnification obligations under Section 10.1 of the MSA **shall be subject to the Liability Cap**."

**Why the SOW controls.** MSA §1.3 ranks the SOW first, ahead of the MSA, for "provisions expressly modifying an identified MSA section." SOW §9.2 expressly identifies and modifies MSA §11.3(a). SOW §1.1 confirms that §1.3 governs conflicts. Nothing in the MSA cures the change, and OF3 cannot override either document because it ranks last.

The result is that, for all coating work under SOW No. 1, the indemnity is capped. That work covers the entire Tarpaulin and Curtain Lines. **We should not advise Zaseil that the MSA carve-out still protects it.**

**Why it matters for Zaseil.**

- **The cap is small relative to the risk.**
  - The Liability Cap is fees paid or payable under the SOW in the 12 months before the claim (§11.2).
  - The Minimum Annual Commitment is $2,400,000 per Contract Year (OF3 §2.1), so the cap is likely in the low single-digit millions.
  - That cap is also aggregate across all claims under the Agreement.
- **The scenario is real.** A single fire involving FR-failed tarpaulins or institutional curtains, including the healthcare-designated Curtain Line styles, could produce death, injury and building-loss claims far above the cap.
- **Lot 2207 is the live risk.** Its retained and *field* samples have already failed CPAI-84 §6 and NFPA 701 TM2 (OF3 ¶2). If any Lot 2207 product is in the field, the uncapped-indemnity question may soon stop being hypothetical.
- **Zaseil keeps the uncovered exposure.** Zaseil (and its downstream customers, who are indemnitees under §10.1) would bear the excess as product seller.
- **The Guaranty does not help.** Guaranty §2.3 limits the Guarantor to Provider's liability and lets it assert every limitation Provider has. The Guarantor therefore benefits from the cap too.

**Mitigating points.** These reduce the exposure but do not cure it.

- **Exceptions that remain uncapped:**
  - §11.3(c) (gross negligence, fraud, willful misconduct) still lifts the cap;
  - §11.3(d) (loss of or damage to Customer Fabric and Finished Goods in Prodous's custody) still lifts the cap.
- **Consequential damages exclusion.** SOW §9.2 refers only to the "Liability Cap." There is a respectable argument that the §11.1 consequential damages exclusion still does not apply to the §10.1 indemnity. We should not rely on that.
- **Insurance.** Prodous must carry:
  - $5M CGL including products-completed operations;
  - $10M umbrella, with Zaseil as additional insured (MSA §12.1–12.2);
  - completed-operations coverage for 3 years after last delivery (SOW §9.3).

  Zaseil's additional-insured status may give it direct access to coverage regardless of the contractual cap. That depends on the endorsement wording, which we have not seen.

**Recommended fix.** *Requires Prodous's agreement* (signed SOW amendment under MSA §§2.4, 16.6).

1. Delete SOW No. 1 §9.2, and conform §9.1 by deleting "except as stated in Section 9.2."
2. Alternatively, amend §9.2 to state that the MSA §11.3(a) carve-out applies in full to Claims arising from Coating Services under the SOW.
3. **Fallback if Prodous resists:** a separate, much higher super-cap for §10.1(a) claims, at least equal to the required insurance limits ($15M), with a clear statement that insurance proceeds are not limited by the cap.
4. Add a rule that no future SOW may modify MSA §11.3(a) unless it says so in a specifically captioned, initialed clause.
5. Meanwhile, obtain the certificates and additional-insured endorsements under MSA §12.2, and confirm the products-completed operations coverage is in force.

---

### Issue 2: Guaranty 45-day Demand window for the Lot 2207 default has expired

**Where:** Guaranty §4.1 (also §§1.2(c), 4.3, 9, 11.3); OF3 Special Terms ¶2.

**What the documents say.**

- **Guaranty §4.1.** The Guarantor "is liable for a Guaranteed Obligation **only if** Beneficiary delivers a Demand to Guarantor **within forty-five (45) days after** Beneficiary first notifies Provider of the Default giving rise to that Guaranteed Obligation."
- **OF3 ¶2.** It records three things:
  - Zaseil delivered its Default Notice to Prodous on **August 3, 2026**, concerning failed FR coating on Lot 2207;
  - "as of the Order Form Date [October 20, 2026], no Demand has been made on the Guarantor"; and
  - Zaseil reserves all rights against Provider and Guarantor.

**Calculation.** August 3, 2026 plus 45 days is **September 17, 2026**. The window closed more than a month before OF3 was signed. It is now nearly two months past.

**Our position on timeliness.** On the face of §4.1, a Demand served today for the August 3 Default would be **untimely**. We should not tell the client otherwise. Prodous Industrial Holdings, Inc. will argue it is released from the Lot 2207 obligations:
- reprocessing, replacement or credit under MSA §6.2;
- damages; and
- any §10.1 indemnity for Lot 2207 field claims.

**Why it matters for Zaseil.**

- **Zaseil loses parent recourse for its only known claim.** If Prodous's own balance sheet is thin, or if Prodous later assigns the Agreement (Issue 4), Zaseil may have no creditworthy party behind the Lot 2207 claims.
- **Provider liability is unaffected.** The Guaranty condition does not release Prodous itself.

**Limits of the reservation of rights.** The OF3 reservation preserves Zaseil's position against *Provider*. It does not bind the Guarantor:
- the Guarantor is not a party to OF3;
- Guaranty §11.3 requires any waiver or amendment of the Guaranty to be signed by both Guarantor and Beneficiary; and
- §4.1 is drafted as a condition to liability, and Delaware courts generally enforce clear conditions precedent as written.

The reservation is still useful. It shows Zaseil never intended to abandon the claim, and it supports the arguments below.

**Arguments available to Zaseil.** These are untested and fact-dependent.

1. **A new Default may start a new window.**
   - The parties have not agreed a §6.2 remedy, and Prodous has not reprocessed, replaced or credited Lot 2207.
   - Prodous's failure to perform its §6.2 remedy obligation, and any later field-failure or third-party Claim, is arguably a *separate* Default giving rise to a *separate* Guaranteed Obligation.
   - Guaranty §4.2 expressly contemplates multiple Demands for multiple Defaults.
   - A fresh written notice to Prodous identifying that new Default, followed within 45 days by a Demand, would start and satisfy a new window for that obligation.
2. **Waiver or estoppel by Guarantor conduct.** This applies if the Guarantor, as parent of Provider, was involved in the root-cause analysis (SOW §8.3) or settlement discussions and led Zaseil to defer a Demand.
3. **Disproportionate forfeiture.** This is an equitable argument against strict enforcement of a short procedural condition where the Guarantor suffered no prejudice. Delaware treats it cautiously. It is a fallback only.
4. **Facts that could make things worse.** We need to confirm whether Zaseil "first notifie[d]" Prodous of the Lot 2207 failure *before* August 3, for example by email or in response to a Provider failed-Lot notice under SOW §5.5. If so, the window may have closed even earlier.

**Recommended fix and next steps.**

1. **Serve a Demand on the Guarantor now.** Deliver it under Guaranty §9:
   - by hand or overnight courier, or by email followed by courier copy;
   - to Prodous Industrial Holdings, Inc., Attn: CFO, with a copy to its General Counsel;
   - with a simultaneous copy to Prodous under §4.3.

   The Demand should:
   - identify the Default and the Guaranteed Obligations (§1.2(c)) and state the amount and performance claimed;
   - expressly rely on the OF3 ¶2 reservation of rights; and
   - preserve all arguments that the Demand is timely or that the condition is excused.

   This does not need anyone's agreement.
2. **Serve a fresh Default notice on Prodous at the same time.** It should identify the continuing failure to perform the §6.2 remedy, and any field issues, as new Defaults. Then serve a further Demand on the Guarantor promptly, well inside 45 days, so a timely Demand exists for those Defaults. This does not need anyone's agreement.
3. **Seek a written acknowledgment or waiver from the Guarantor.** It should state that the Guarantor will not assert §4.1 for Lot 2207 and that the Guaranty covers those obligations. *This requires the Guarantor's signed agreement* (Guaranty §11.3). It can be packaged with the Issue 3 consent negotiation.
4. **Process fix going forward.**
   - Seek to amend §4.1, by removing the condition or extending it to at least one year with a clear statement that late Demand releases the Guarantor only to the extent of actual prejudice. *This requires the Guarantor's agreement.*
   - Internally, docket a Demand to the Guarantor the same day as every future default notice to Prodous.

---

### Issue 3: Kestrel merger triggers Prodous's Change of Control consent right, and no consent has been obtained

**Where:** MSA §14.3 (with §§1.4(b), 14.1); OF3 §2.5 and Special Terms ¶1.

**What the documents say.**

- **OF3 ¶1.** It records Zaseil's Agreement and Plan of Merger with **Kestrel Fiberworks Group, Inc.** dated October 1, 2026, under which Zaseil will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Kestrel. Closing is expected **December 1, 2026**.
- **Change of Control definition (MSA §1.4(b)).** The transaction falls within it twice over:
  - Zaseil is a constituent entity in a merger (clause (i)); and
  - Kestrel will acquire more than 50% of Zaseil's voting securities (clause (ii)).
- **MSA §14.3.** A Change of Control of Customer "is **deemed an assignment by Customer** requiring Provider's prior written consent under Section 14.1." If the Change of Control occurs without consent:
  - Prodous may terminate the Agreement and **all** SOWs by notice; and
  - Zaseil must pay the **Early Termination Fee** within 30 days.
- **The Early Termination Fee (OF3 §2.5).** It equals the Minimum Annual Commitment ($2,400,000) for the Contract Year in which termination takes effect, less the amounts counted under OF3 §2.2 through termination.

**No consent in the folder.** Neither OF3 ¶1 nor anything else in the folder records Prodous's consent.
- OF3 ¶1 is a disclosure by Customer, not a consent or waiver by Provider.
- MSA §16.6 requires any waiver to be in a writing signed by the waiving party.
- Prodous's signature on OF3, which says the MAC and tiers "remain unchanged," arguably shows Prodous knows of and accepts the deal. That is an argument, not a consent.

**Why it matters for Zaseil.**

- **Prodous gains a walk-away right at closing.** It could:
  - terminate all coating work under SOW No. 1, which covers Zaseil's entire tarpaulin and curtain FR finishing, mid-year; and
  - collect the unearned balance of the $2.4M Minimum Annual Commitment.
- **Supply disruption would follow.** Requalification at a substitute coater (compare SOW §5.4, which requires three passing independent-lab qualification Lots) would take months.
- **Prodous gets leverage in the Lot 2207 dispute and on pricing.** MSA §14.1 has no "not to be unreasonably withheld" qualifier, so Prodous may condition or refuse consent.
- **There is deal-level risk.** The merger agreement likely contains representations or covenants on third-party consents for material contracts. An unconsented Change of Control could affect closing conditions or create indemnity exposure to Kestrel.

**Recommended fix.** *Requires Prodous's agreement.*

1. **Obtain Prodous's prior written consent before the December 1, 2026 closing.** It should be a short signed letter or amendment that:
   - consents to the Kestrel merger;
   - waives the §14.3 termination right and the Early Termination Fee for this transaction; and
   - confirms the Agreement, SOW No. 1 and OF3 continue unchanged.
2. **Better, amend MSA §14.3** to delete it or carve out Changes of Control. If not deleted, §14.1 should at minimum be amended so consent "may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed." Assignment to an Affiliate or successor by merger should also be permitted without consent. This would mirror NDA §10.4, which already permits merger-successor assignment.
3. **Package the asks.** Prodous wants continued volume after closing, which OF3 ¶1 says Zaseil expects to provide. That is Zaseil's leverage. One amendment could cover Issues 1, 3 and 4, plus a Guarantor joinder or acknowledgment for Issues 2 and 4.
4. **If consent cannot be obtained before closing,** consider with M&A deal counsel whether closing should be conditioned on it or the date moved. Quantify the Early Termination Fee as of December 1 (see Part V).
5. **Comply with notice.** Give the post-closing notice required by OF3 ¶1 within 5 business days after closing.

---

### Issue 4: Prodous may assign freely, including to a Zaseil competitor, and any permitted assignment terminates the Guaranty

**Where:** MSA §14.2 (compare §14.1); Guaranty §6.2 (and §6.3).

**What the documents say.**

- **MSA §14.2.** Prodous "may assign or transfer the Agreement or any SOW, in whole or in part, to any person **without Customer's consent**, upon written notice to Customer." Nothing excludes competitors of Zaseil, unaffiliated buyers, or thinly capitalized assignees.
- **The contrast with §14.1.** Zaseil cannot assign at all without Prodous's consent.
- **Guaranty §6.2.** The Guaranty "terminates automatically, without further action by any person, on any assignment or transfer by Provider ... that is permitted under the MSA." A partial assignment, even of one SOW, terminates the Guaranty "as to the Agreement as a whole."
- **Every assignment is "permitted."** Because §14.2 permits every assignment, any assignment by Prodous ends the parent credit support.
- **Accrued Demands may be lost too.** Guaranty §6.3 preserves pre-expiration Demands only "subject to Sections 4 and 6.2." This suggests a §6.2 termination may cut off Demands already made, including any Lot 2207 Demand.

**Why it matters for Zaseil.**

- **Competitor risk.** Prodous could transfer the Zaseil work, along with the Customer Process Information, Schedule A formulations, cure profiles and volumes it holds (MSA §8.2), to a Zaseil competitor or a competitor's affiliate.
  - MSA §8.2 and §9 restrict use and disclosure, but the assignee would step into Prodous's shoes and legitimately hold that know-how.
- **Credit risk.** Prodous could move the contract to a shell or financially weak entity. The Guaranty from Prodous Industrial Holdings, Inc. would end at the same moment. Zaseil would be left with:
  - indemnity, warranty (24-month and 36-month durability) and Lot 2207 claims against a party that may be unable to pay; and
  - no parent recourse.
- **It undercuts other protections.**
  - It sidesteps the MSA §2.3 bar on subcontracting without consent.
  - It may sidestep the facility and requalification protections in MSA §2.2 and SOW §2.2 and §5.4, depending on the assignee's plant.
- **No defensive option.** Zaseil cannot block the assignment. Its only response is termination for breach or insolvency, if grounds exist.

**Recommended fix.**

1. **Amend MSA §14.2.** It should prohibit assignment by Provider without Customer's prior written consent.
   - At most, permit one carve-out: assignment to a successor to all or substantially all of Provider's coating business that (a) is not a Zaseil competitor or competitor affiliate, (b) has net worth at least equal to Provider's at signing, (c) assumes the Agreement in writing, and (d) performs at the same Facility, or completes requalification first.
   - Add that any purported assignment in breach of §14.2 is void, mirroring §14.1.
   - *Requires Prodous's agreement.*
2. **Amend Guaranty §6.2.** It should state that the Guaranty continues in full force after any assignment or transfer by Provider and extends to the assignee's obligations. Alternatively, no assignment should be effective until a replacement guaranty acceptable to Zaseil is delivered. Fix §6.3 so accrued Demands survive any termination.
   - *Requires the Guarantor's signed agreement* (Guaranty §11.3). Prodous's signature on the MSA amendment is not enough.
3. **Confirm with the client** that Prodous has not already given a §14.2 notice of any assignment or transfer.

---

## III. Additional Observations (lower priority)

- **Missing Order Forms.** OF3 is "No. 3." Order Forms No. 1 and No. 2 are not in the folder. They may contain earlier commercial terms, an earlier or different Early Termination Fee, or relevant waivers. OF3 §1.3 applies only to POs issued on or after October 20, 2026. Yet OF3 §2.1 counts the full Contract Year starting March 2, 2026 toward the MAC and fixes the Early Termination Fee by reference to it. We need to confirm how the earlier Order Forms interact.
- **OF3 is lowest in precedence (MSA §1.3).** Nothing in OF3's Special Terms can override the MSA or SOW. That is another reason the OF3 reservation and merger disclosure cannot cure Issues 2 and 3 on their own.
- **Lot 2207 preservation.** OF3 ¶3 helpfully requires Prodous to quarantine Lot 2207 samples and records. Zaseil should exercise its MSA §5.4 audit right and obtain independent lab testing under SOW §5.3 now, while the material is preserved.
- **Missing schedules.** SOW Schedules A (Style Specifications) and B (Processing Fees) are "attached separately" and are not in the folder.
- **Unsigned copies.** All folder copies have blank signature blocks. We should confirm executed versions exist and match.

## IV. Mutual NDA

I reviewed the NDA (January 12, 2026), and it raises no issue requiring action.

- **Coverage.** It covers pre-MSA evaluation disclosures. Its disclosure period runs to January 12, 2028, with obligations surviving 3 more years, and indefinitely for trade secrets.
- **Relationship to the MSA.** Confidentiality for the commercial relationship is now principally governed by MSA §9. MSA §8.2 treats Customer Process Information as Zaseil's confidential information.
- **Assignment clause.** NDA §10.4 permits merger-successor assignment by either party. It does not alter MSA §§14.1–14.3, which are separate and stricter.
- **Merger diligence.** Zaseil should confirm that any disclosure of Prodous information to Kestrel in diligence fit within the "Representatives"/need-to-know limits. I saw nothing indicating a problem.

## V. Open Items: What We Need from the Client

1. **Default Notice details.** We need a copy of the August 3, 2026 Default Notice and proof of delivery. We also need any earlier communications to Prodous about the Lot 2207 failure, including Provider failed-Lot notices under SOW §5.5, emails and calls. These determine when Zaseil "first notifie[d]" Provider (Guaranty §4.1) and whether the window closed even before September 17.
2. **Any contact with the Guarantor.** We need any communication from Zaseil to Prodous Industrial Holdings, Inc. since August 3 that might qualify as, or support, a Demand, waiver or estoppel argument. We also need to know whether Guarantor personnel took part in the root-cause or remedy discussions.
3. **Lot 2207 field status.** Where did Lot 2207 product ship? Is it in the field? Have there been any fire incidents, customer complaints, recalls or third-party Claims? This bears directly on Issues 1 and 2.
4. **Early Termination Fee inputs.** We need the fees invoiced under SOW No. 1 from March 2, 2026 to date, net of §6.4 credits, plus any §6.2(c) credits. With these we can quantify the Early Termination Fee as of December 1, 2026 and estimate the current Liability Cap.
5. **Merger documents.** We need the Kestrel merger agreement provisions on third-party consents, material contracts and closing conditions. We should also ask whether Kestrel or deal counsel has flagged the Prodous contract, and whether any approach to Prodous has been made.
6. **Kestrel's position.** Does Kestrel have its own coating suppliers, or an interest in moving the work? This bears on negotiating leverage and on the Issue 4 competitor carve-out.
7. **Insurance documents.** We need Prodous's certificates of insurance and additional-insured endorsements (MSA §12.2).
8. **Missing documents.** We need Order Forms No. 1 and No. 2, SOW Schedules A and B, and executed copies of all documents.
9. **Prodous's finances.** Do we have any information on Prodous's financial condition? Has Prodous given notice of any assignment (MSA §14.2) or of any event affecting the Guarantor (MSA §15.2)?

## VI. Recommended Immediate Steps (this week)

1. Serve a Demand on the Guarantor for Lot 2207, together with a fresh default notice to Prodous for the continuing failure to remedy, and a follow-on Demand (Issue 2). *No counterparty agreement needed.*
2. Open negotiations with Prodous and the Guarantor on a single amendment package. *Requires agreement of Prodous and, for the Guaranty items, the Guarantor.* The package should cover:
   - written consent to the Kestrel Change of Control and waiver of the Early Termination Fee for it (Issue 3);
   - deletion of SOW §9.2 (Issue 1);
   - amendment of MSA §14.2 and Guaranty §6.2 (Issue 4); and
   - a Guarantor acknowledgment that §4.1 will not be asserted for Lot 2207 (Issue 2).
3. Coordinate with M&A deal counsel on the December 1 closing timeline in light of the consent requirement.
4. Collect the client information listed in Part V.

## II. Issues (Ranked)

### Issue 1: Change of Control from the Kestrel Merger Requires Prodous's Consent, Which Has Not Been Obtained

**Where it appears**
- MSA § 14.3 (Change of Control of Customer).
- MSA § 14.1 (Customer may not assign without Provider's prior written consent; a non-compliant assignment is void).
- MSA § 1.4(b) (definition of Change of Control).
- Order Form § 2.5 (Early Termination Fee) and § 5, Special Terms ¶ 1 (Kestrel Transaction).

**What the documents say**
- Order Form ¶ 1 records an Agreement and Plan of Merger dated October 1, 2026 between Zaseil and Kestrel Fiberworks Group, Inc. Under it, Zaseil will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Kestrel, with closing expected December 1, 2026.
- That transaction is a Change of Control under MSA § 1.4(b):
  - under clause (i), because it is a merger in which Zaseil is a constituent entity; and
  - under clause (ii), because Kestrel will acquire more than 50% of Zaseil's voting securities.
- MSA § 14.3 deems a Change of Control of Customer "an assignment by Customer requiring Provider's prior written consent under Section 14.1."
- The Order Form only *advises* Prodous of the merger and commits Zaseil to give post-closing notice. It does not record Prodous's consent, and it does not waive § 14.3.
- MSA § 16.6 requires any waiver to be in writing and signed by the waiving party. Prodous's signature on an Order Form that merely describes the transaction is therefore unlikely to operate as consent.
- No consent from Prodous appears anywhere in the folder.

**Why it matters for Zaseil**
- If the merger closes without consent, Prodous may terminate the Agreement and all SOWs by written notice.
- Zaseil must then pay the Early Termination Fee within 30 days.
- Under Order Form § 2.5, the Early Termination Fee is the $2,400,000 Minimum Annual Commitment for the Contract Year in which termination takes effect, less the amounts counted under § 2.2 through the termination date. The current Contract Year runs March 2, 2026 through March 1, 2027.
- If Zaseil's year-to-date counted fees are low, the fee could be a substantial part of $2.4 million.
- Zaseil would also lose its reserved coating capacity of 180,000 linear yards per month (SOW § 6.3) on short notice. It would have to requalify a new coater for FR-critical product lines.
- The consent right also gives Prodous leverage just before closing. Prodous could use it to extract price or term concessions, including on Issues 2 and 3.
- Separately, the merger agreement may contain representations, covenants or closing conditions about third-party consents under material contracts. A missing consent could create exposure to Kestrel as well.

**Recommended fix**
- **Obtain Prodous's written consent to the Kestrel Change of Control before the December 1, 2026 closing.** Ideally, the consent should be a short signed amendment under MSA § 16.6 that:
  - expressly consents to the Kestrel merger under §§ 14.1 and 14.3;
  - confirms Prodous will not terminate or claim the Early Termination Fee on account of it; and
  - preferably deletes § 14.3 or narrows it, for example to an acquisition by a direct competitor of Prodous.
- **Requires Prodous's agreement.** Zaseil cannot cure this unilaterally.
- **Consider the Guarantor.** Zaseil remains the Beneficiary after a reverse-subsidiary merger, so the Guarantor's signature is not strictly required. However, a Guarantor acknowledgment that the Guaranty continues for Zaseil after closing is low-cost comfort.
- **Fallback if consent cannot be obtained before closing:**
  - quantify the Early Termination Fee exposure;
  - raise the issue with Kestrel so the parties can allocate the risk or adjust closing mechanics; and
  - consider whether to seek a short pre-closing standstill from Prodous.

### Issue 2: SOW No. 1 Caps Prodous's Third-Party Bodily Injury and Property Damage Indemnity, and the SOW Controls

**Where it appears**
- SOW § 9.2 (Indemnity for Coating Services), read with SOW § 9.1.
- MSA § 1.3 (Order of Precedence).
- MSA § 10.1 (Provider indemnity).
- MSA § 11.2 (Liability Cap).
- MSA § 11.3(a) (indemnity carve-out from the cap).

**What the documents say**
- MSA § 10.1(a) requires Prodous to indemnify Zaseil, its Affiliates and its customers against third-party Claims for bodily injury, death and property damage. This covers injury and damage caused by the Services, the Finished Goods as processed, or "any failure of the FR coatings applied by Provider to meet the Specifications."
- MSA § 11.3(a) carves those indemnity obligations out of the § 11.2 Liability Cap. The Liability Cap is the fees paid or payable under the applicable SOW in the 12 months preceding the claim.
- SOW § 9.2 then provides that, "[w]ith respect to Section 11.3(a) of the MSA," for Claims arising from Coating Services under the SOW, Prodous's § 10.1 indemnification obligations "**shall be subject to the Liability Cap**."
- MSA § 1.3 puts the SOW first in the order of precedence, but only for "provisions expressly modifying an identified MSA section." SOW § 9.2 expressly identifies and modifies § 11.3(a). It therefore meets that test and prevails over the MSA carve-out. SOW §§ 1.1 and 9.1 confirm the structure.
- **Result:** for all coating work under SOW No. 1, which is currently all of the work, the third-party injury and property damage indemnity is capped at 12 months of SOW fees. It is not uncapped.

**Why it matters for Zaseil**
- This is Zaseil's largest exposure in the relationship. The SOW covers tarpaulins tested to CPAI-84 and NFPA 701, and curtain and divider fabrics for commercial, institutional and healthcare settings.
- An FR coating failure can lead to fire-related bodily injury, wrongful death and property damage claims. Those claims could be brought against Zaseil and its customers, whom § 10.1 also protects. They could far exceed one year of processing fees.
- With the Minimum Annual Commitment at $2.4 million, the cap is likely in the low single-digit millions at most. It would be shared across all claims in aggregate.
- Lot 2207 has already failed CPAI-84 § 6 and NFPA 701 Test Method 2 in both retained and *field* samples (Order Form ¶ 2). That makes this risk concrete rather than theoretical. Any third-party claim from Lot 2207 product in the field would fall within the capped indemnity.
- The Guaranty does not help. Guaranty § 2.3 lets the Guarantor assert any limitation Prodous could assert, including the Liability Cap.
- **Partial mitigants:**
  - MSA § 11.3(c) still leaves gross negligence, fraud and willful misconduct uncapped.
  - Zaseil is an additional insured on Prodous's CGL policy ($5M) and umbrella policy ($10M) under MSA § 12.2, and SOW § 9.3 extends products-completed operations coverage for three years after the last delivery. That gives some direct insurance recourse.
  - However, insurance limits and the cap are separate questions. Coverage depends on the policy terms, which we have not seen.

**Recommended fix**
- **Delete SOW § 9.2,** or replace it with language confirming that MSA § 11.3(a) applies in full to Coating Services under the SOW.
- **Fallback:** a separate, substantially higher super-cap for § 10.1(a) claims, at least equal to Prodous's combined CGL and umbrella limits ($15 million), with a requirement that insurance proceeds are not counted against it.
- **Requires Prodous's agreement.** The SOW can be amended only by a signed writing (MSA §§ 2.4, 16.6).
- **Consider the Guarantor.** Guaranty § 5.2(a) allows amendments without Guarantor consent, and Guaranty § 2.3 tracks Provider's liability. A Guarantor acknowledgment is still advisable for clarity.
- **Leverage:** raise this together with the Issue 1 consent request.

### Issue 3: The Guaranty's 45-Day Demand Window for the Lot 2207 Default Has Expired

**Where it appears**
- Guaranty § 4.1 (Condition to Liability), with §§ 1.2(c), 4.3, 9 and 11.3.
- Order Form § 5, Special Terms ¶ 2 (Lot 2207 Default Notice).

**What the documents say**
- Guaranty § 4.1 makes the Guarantor, Prodous Industrial Holdings, Inc., liable for a Guaranteed Obligation "only if" Zaseil delivers a Demand "**within forty-five (45) days** after Beneficiary first notifies Provider of the Default."
- Order Form ¶ 2 records three facts:
  - Zaseil delivered its Default Notice for the defective FR coating on Lot 2207 on **August 3, 2026**;
  - as of October 20, 2026, **no Demand had been made** on the Guarantor; and
  - Zaseil reserved all rights against Provider and the Guarantor.
- Forty-five days from August 3, 2026 ended on **September 17, 2026**. The window had closed more than a month before the Order Form was signed.
- Nothing in the MSA, SOW or Order Form extends or overrides the condition.
- **A Demand served now would not be timely under § 4.1.**

**Why it matters for Zaseil**
- The Guarantor will argue that it is released from liability for the Lot 2207 Guaranteed Obligations. Those obligations include:
  - Prodous's remedy obligations under MSA § 6.2 (reprocessing, replacing Customer Fabric at replacement cost, or a credit or refund);
  - damages; and
  - possibly any indemnity obligation arising from third-party claims tied to Lot 2207.
- If that argument succeeds, Zaseil's recourse for Lot 2207 is limited to Prodous Coating Services LLC alone, and the parent credit support is lost.
- This matters most if the Lot 2207 dispute escalates, or if Prodous's own balance sheet is thin. We have no financial information on Prodous.
- The reservation of rights in Order Form ¶ 2 protects Zaseil against an argument that it *waived* its rights by signing the Order Form or continuing to perform. It does not, by itself, satisfy or excuse a condition precedent in a document the Guarantor signed. Delaware courts generally enforce express conditions precedent as written.
- In addition, Guaranty § 11.3 requires any waiver to be in writing and signed by both Guarantor and Beneficiary. The Guarantor is not a party to the Order Form.

**Recommended fix / next steps**
1. **Serve a Demand on the Guarantor immediately.** The Demand should:
   - comply with Guaranty §§ 1.2(c), 4.3 and 9;
   - be delivered to the CFO with a copy to General Counsel, by hand, overnight courier, or email followed by courier;
   - be copied simultaneously to Prodous;
   - identify the Lot 2207 Default and the Guaranteed Obligations; and
   - expressly rely on the Order Form ¶ 2 reservation of rights.

   This does not make the Demand timely. It preserves Zaseil's position and starts the 10-business-day performance period under § 2.2 if the condition is excused or waived.
2. **Seek a written acknowledgment or waiver from the Guarantor** under Guaranty § 11.3. The waiver should confirm that the § 4.1 condition is waived or deemed satisfied for Lot 2207. **This requires the Guarantor's agreement.** Consider packaging it with the Issue 1 consent and the Issue 2 amendment.
3. **Preserve alternative arguments**, for use only if the Guarantor refuses:
   - **Separate Defaults.** Under Guaranty § 4.2, a later and separate Default, such as Prodous's failure to provide the § 6.2 remedy now that the parties have deadlocked, or a future failure to indemnify a third-party Claim, may support a fresh notice to Prodous and a timely Demand within 45 days of it.
   - **Excuse or forfeiture.** Excuse of the condition, or disproportionate forfeiture, if facts support it.

   These arguments are uncertain and should not be relied on as the primary strategy.
4. **Prospectively,** amend Guaranty § 4.1 to delete the time-bar or lengthen it substantially, for example to 12 months. **This requires the Guarantor's agreement.** Put in place an internal docketing procedure so that any future default notice to Prodous automatically triggers a Demand to the Guarantor.

## III. Mutual NDA (No Action Required)

- The January 12, 2026 NDA governed pre-contract evaluation discussions.
- Confidentiality of Customer Process Information under the commercial relationship is now covered more specifically by MSA §§ 8.2 and 9. The MSA protection lasts five years after termination and indefinitely for trade secrets.
- The NDA's disclosure period runs to January 12, 2028, so it overlaps with the MSA. I see no conflict that disadvantages Zaseil.
- The NDA's assignment clause (§ 10.4) permits assignment to a successor by merger on notice, so the Kestrel transaction raises no NDA consent issue.
- No changes are recommended.
